Commentary.Commentary: The South Africans get into a huddle. Very few runs to defend. But can they take a few wickets for psychological advantage heading into the second Test? The players now disperse from the huddle. Kagiso Rabada will start off proceedings. Imran Butt and Abid Ali are the openers for Pakistan. Butt to face. Just under 25 minutes to go to Lunch.
... FINAL INNINGS ...

Believe. That is what Pakistan's mantra has been. They were finding it difficult to get wickets on Thursday but they kept believing that one wicket will open the floodgates and it did. Rassie van der Dussen fell after a century stand and the door burst open. Everyone did well, with Yasir enjoying the conditions, but the most impressive was Nauman Ali. 12th Pakistan bowler to take a 5-fer on debut and the only left-arm spinner in that list! Terrific. He finishes with 7 in the match.

Yeah, well, South Africa will rue the last few overs of their batting. 175/1 at one stage. 192/6 it became, in the span of 68 balls. Game turned. The top 3 batters had raised hopes of setting up a good total, putting up a good fight, but the middle order simply crumbled like a cookie. And it is happening way too often. This morning, the Proteas were 187/4, but have lost their last 6 wickets for just 58 runs. Combination of playing from the crease, not able to adjust to the rough and being consumed by spin.

The two fat ladies. That is what Pakistan are after. Oh relax. It is the number 88, which is called so. Pakistan have got 5 sessions and a bit more to take a 1-0 series lead. Wonderful comeback since Thursday afternoon.

PITCH REPORT - Mike Haysman more or less talks about the game and very less about the actual deck. He eventually points out to a good length area where there is some rough, outside the left-hander's off stump. There will be turn for sure.

Pakistan will be happy but they need to be focused. They saw what their batsmen did, to recover from 27/4. South Africa still have some batting to come and if they get a couple of good sessions, the hosts will be back under pressure, as it is Pakistan who will be batting last. So they need to pick the remaining 6 wickets quickly. How will the Saffas play? They are roughly 150 runs away from worrying Pakistan. But how will they get there? Attack on a turning pitch? Or just bat defensively and ensure that wickets are not lost? They need to mix caution with aggression. Because if they just get into wicket-saving mode, then that passage of 30 minutes which happened on Thursday, could happen again and this Test might end today itself.

The last session of Thursday was when it began. Balls staying low, puff of dust emanating from the pitch, reverse swing, you name it. The batters found it difficult to negotiate and the effect was seen. Edges were taken and they either went in gaps or were put down. But it did not take long for Lionel Messi to strike. Ah okay... the look-alike then. Yasir Shah persisted with his line and length and along with Nauman Ali, picked up 3 wickets in the span of 33 balls. The game changed complexion massively. South Africa were perhaps looking at ending the day at 40-odd ahead for the loss of a wicket, but are effectively 29/4 instead. Ohhh those nervous 30 minutes before the close!

Hard to be in the Protea camp right now. They started Day 4 poorly, but then came back splendidly well through the top 3 batsmen. The fightback was dogged and determined, with the score reading 175/1 and the visitors erasing the deficit. But then, calamity struck. In Asia, things don't seem to happen for a long time in Tests. And then when they happen, everything cuts loose.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the first Test between South Africa and Pakistan. The moving day of the match saw Pakistan gain a handy 158-run lead in their first innings with the tail adding 83 runs for the last 2 wickets.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1...

So, Yasir Shah now has 3 wickets and Nauman Ali has 1. Both were looking very threatening towards the end and when Pakistan step out on Day 4, they will be looking to keep the pressure up on South Africa and will try to bundle them out as quickly as possible. Can Quinton de Kock rise to the occasion though, alongwith the rest, to put up a fight? Let's find out. Join us on Friday, 29th January 2021, at 1000 Local (0500 GMT) to find out. Until then, take care and cheers...

In the second session too the openers were doing well before Dean was bruised badly on the gloves from an Afridi delivery that just took off from the rough. That made Elgar uncomfortable afterwards. In the end, he perished to Yasir. After that though, there was a good long stand of 127 runs between Aiden and Van der Dussen, wherein both batsmen got to their fifties. However, as the day was nearing its end, Pakistan came back, and took 3 wickets on the trot, pushing the tourists on the back foot.

Earlier, Pakistan started the day, with two wickets still remaining. Kagiso had gotten rid of Hasan Ali for his 200th wicket in Tests but there was a good 55-run stand for the 10th wicket, before Nauman Ali fell. Pakistan had garnered a good lead of 158. Stepping out to bat in response to that, the South Africans braved the first session well.

Right then, South Africa were looking good but one moment, one moment is all and they now end Day 3 on the back foot. They lost 3 wickets on a spree towards the end of the Day and end the day, effectively at 29/4. They would need to put up a good batting performance tomorrow. Pakistan, meanwhile, would be excited and why not! They were superb with the ball towards the end.

Prods forward and keeps this one out.
Rassie does what he did on the previous delivery again.
Loopy on leg, RvdD pads this one too.
Short and on middle, clipped to the leg side for a single.
Flighted on leg, spins back in sharply, Aiden looks to pad this one away but he misses and the ball goes to the first slip.
Flighted on leg, AM pads this one away.
Drives this one through the cover region, does Rassie van der Dussen. Picks up a couple. Saffas are leading by 9 runs now.
Rassie has just watchfully blocked this out.
Short of a length and on middle, AM flicks this one to square leg. One run.
On off, defended back.
Around off on a good length, Aiden pushes this one out towards the cover region.
Worked with a straight bat to the leg side.
Loopy on leg, padded away by RvdD. Three runs from this over.
Shortish and on off, Markram pulls this one through mid-wicket. Hasan Ali does well to chase after this one and drags it before the ropes. Three this time.

An appeal for lbw but not entertained by the umpire. Flighted on leg and middle, Aiden looks to block but misses and gets rapped on the pads. An appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Pitched outside leg probably.
Loopy on middle, tucked to the mid-wicket region.
Loopy on leg, Aiden pads this one away.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler.

EDGY FOUR. SOUTH AFRICA LEAD BY 3 RUNS NOW. Lucky boundary, but the Saffas will accept this one gleefully. Length and outside off, Rassie looks to push this one to the off side but the ball takes the outside edge and goes to the third man region for a boundary.
Pushed to the cover region, safely, off the upper part of the bat.
On middle, flicked to short mid-wicket.
Around off on a good length, pushed to covers.
EDGED...DOES NOT CARRY. On a length and around off, van der Dussen looks to push this one away but the ball takes an outside edge and goes on the bounce to the keeper.

NOT OUT! Sliding down the leg side. Ashraf bowls a good length delivery around the middle and leg pole, van der Dussen looks to pull this one to the leg side but he misses and gets rapped on the pads. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Rassie goes for the review straightaway. Ultra Edge shows no bat is involved. Ball Tracker comes in and there are 2 reds but this one is going down the leg side. Saffas retain their review and the on-field decision is overturned.
Review time! There is a player review, from Rassie's side for a LBW. What does technology have to say? Will van der Dussen survive?
Faheem Ashraf is back. 3-2-1-0 are Faheem's figures so far.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Flatter and on middle, Aiden goes on his back foot and tucks this one to the mid-wicket region.
Floated down the leg side, AM comes forward looking to pad this one away but he misses and the ball goes to the keeper.
Shortish and on leg again, Aiden again pads this one away.
Flatter on leg, AM pads this one away.
FOUR! A good way to start after the mini-break. Flighted and around off, Markram powers this one slightly uppishly through the extra cover region for a boundary. Behind by 1 run now.
Lovely ball! A superb delivery from Hasan here. He bowls a yorker on off and middle, Aiden brings his bat down and digs it out, off the inner half, to the backward square leg region, for a single.

Final DRINKS break of the day. South Africa, all the way, based on how they are batting. It is because of Markram and van der Dussen that the visitors are just trailing by 5 runs. They have been making the bowlers toil hard and have not given any easy chances to Pakistan and have also added 69 runs to the score after the Tea break. The hosts, would atleast want a couple of wickets before Stumps and that is what they will be aiming to do in the last phase of play for Day 3.
Very full length ball on the stumps, blocked back on the turf.
NO BALL! Hasan Ali goes past the crease, at the non-striker's end here. That is solidly defended off the front foot.
Full and on the stumps, solidly blocked to the off side.
Short of a length and outside off, defended to the off side for a single.
FOUR! This is beautifully played. Full length ball on middle, van der Dussen clips it and clips it nicely through square leg for a boundary.

50 FOR RASSIE! Job well done. Remarkable. Full length ball on middle and leg, van der Dussen pushes it wide of the bowler, to the mid on region. The fielder runs and stops that. A couple for Rassie to get to his half ton.
Flatter and on the pads, no shot offered and it is padded away to the leg side.

BEATEN! BEAUTY! Looped up delivery outside off, Aiden lets out a big stride forward, in defence, but misses. The keeper collects and whips the bails off but Markram had his back foot inside the line there.
On the pads, Markram does not offer a shot and ends up wearing it on his pads.
Tosses this one outside off, Markram is happy to pad that one away.
Floated on middle and leg, solid defense from Aiden.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

A huge appeal for LBW but not given. Height was an issue perhaps. No review from Pakistan, perhaps keeping the height factor in mind. Good length ball around off, van der Dussen comes forward in defence but misses and is hit in the pads. There is a loud shout for lbw but the umpire, Aleem Dar, is unmoved. No review and so, we move on.
Full length ball around off, Rassie keeps this out on the off side.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Good length ball on the stumps, van der Dussen defends it back on the track.

FOUR! Nicely put away in the gap. Rassie moves to 49 now. Shortish length ball around off, Rassie van der Dussen swings it through square leg. The fielder in the deep runs to his right but it was hit well wide of him and a boundary results.
Full and around off, poked to the off side.
Shortish length delivery on middle, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
On the pads, clipped through square leg for a single.
Down the leg side, Rassie rocks back but ends up leaving it. Rizwan fails to collect it cleanly and it goes behind. Skipper Azam goes to fetch that and South Africa decide against the run there.
Comes forward and pushes this loopy one past silly point safely as a few Pakistan players shouted 'Catch it'.
Fullish length delivery, kept out back on the track.
Looped up and around off, Rassie comes forward in defense.
FOUR! That is a lovely shot. Shot of the innings. Pleasing to watch. Full length delivery on middle and leg, Aiden drives it straight and past the bowler and gets a boundary.

Lovely piece of hitting this, from Rassie van der Dussen. Did not overhit that at all. Full and outside off, RvdD comes forward and drives it through the covers. Azhar gives chase, dives as the ball nears the ropes and keeps it out. Three taken though.
Full ball, van der Dussen presents a straight bat and defends it out to mid on. Hang on, no ball called here. Hasan has overstepped.
Outside off, dabbed to the off side. Rassie comes down, looking for a single, but is sent back.
Nicely played. On the pads, Markram rolls his wrists nicely and flicks it down to fine leg for a single.
Full length ball around the off pole, Aiden blocks it out on the off side. Says 'no' to his partner for a single.
Full length delivery around off, defended to the off side.
Flighted and on off, RvdD pushes this one to the point region.
Van der Dussen does exactly what he did on the last delivery.
Rassie plays this one to the cover region.
Comes on the front foot and blocks this one.

An appeal for lbw but turned down. Flighted on off and middle, Rassie comes on his front foot and looks to block but it takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads. There players enquire but the umpire says no. They do not opt for the review as well.

FOUR OVERTHROWS. Shaheen is the culprit. Flighted on middle, van der Dussen flicks this one to the mid-wicket region. Shaheen collects and has a shy at the non-striker's end but he misses. There is no one backing up and the ball runs away to the ropes.
Tucked to the square leg region. 5 off this over. Partnership is now at 78.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR. Beautiful stroke. Markram plays this one so well. On a full length and on middle, Aiden clips this one through mid-wicket and there is no point in chasing after this one, the ball just zips away past the ropes.
Outside off, AM punches this one to covers.
Length and on off, Rassie flicks this one to the right of mid on, where the fielder makes a good diving stop. One run.
On a length and around the off pole, RvdD pushes this one to the cover region.
Hasan Ali is back here. 8-1-23-0 to him so far.
Flighted on off, AM pushes it back to the bowler.
Markram blocks this one solidly off the front foot.
Loopy on middle, flicked to the leg side.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
No Ball. On off, Aiden plays this to covers again. Ali has overstepped and this will be a No Ball.
Floated and around off this time, Aiden pushes this one to covers.
Flighted around off, blocked.
Nauman Ali coming on to bowl. 7-2-9-0 are Ali's figures so far.
EDGY. On a good length and on middle, Rassie looks to flick this one to the leg side but the ball takes the leading edge and goes towards the gully fielder.
Gets his bat down and defends this one back onto the turf.
On the middle pole, RvdD clips this one to deep square leg. A couple of runs this time.

FIFTY FOR AIDEN MARKRAM. He has batted beautifully and has delivered a top quality knock under pressure. It is also his first 50 in the sub-continent region. A back of a length ball on middle, Markram clips this one to the fine leg region for a single.

FOUR! There were shouts of 'Catch it' but it went over the fielder there. Aiden moves to 49 now. Fuller and around off, Markram lofts this one over the cover region and the ball speeds away to the ropes.
Worked with a closed-face bat towards the mid-wicket region.
Driven but straight to the fielder stationed at covers. 3 runs off this over.
On off, flicked to the leg side.

NOT OUT! Easy work for the third umpire. Shortish and around off, Aiden punches this one towards the mid off region. The batters take off for the single and the fielder collects the ball and has a shy at the non-striker's end and hits. The third umpire is called for and replays show that Markram's bat was grounded well as the bails came off. One run.
The third umpire is called into play to check this run out appeal. Clearly not out.
Flatter and on the pads, flicked to short fine leg for a single.
Front foot defense is on display here by RvdD.
Drags his length back and bowls this short and around off, Aiden punches this one to wide mid off for a single.
On the pads, AM hops and tucks this one to the deep square leg region for a single.
Length and around off, Aiden pushes this one towards the cover-point region. Afridi falls in his followthrough as well. But no harm. All good to continue.
On a fuller length and on the middle pole, Rassie flicks this one through square leg for a single.
On a length and outside the off pole, Rassie van der Dussen just leaves it alone.
Back of a length and around off, van der Dussen taps this one towards point. Is quick to yell 'no' for the single.

FOUR! Worked nicely through the covers. This outfield is very quick. Shaheen just venturing full enough, outside off, Rassie comes forward and leans into the drive. Sends it through the covers. Two fielders give chase but neither had any chance there as the ball races away for a boundary.
Outside off, stroked through cover-point for a single.
Shortish and around off, Aiden swings it through square leg, to the man in the deep. It does not have enough on it to reach the fence there and hence they take three.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Flatter and around off, it is pushed down to mid on. The length was dragged back by Yasir here.
Full and on middle and off, blocked back to the bowler.
Outside off, defended to the off side.
A couple and 100 is on the board now, as well. On middle, clipped through the mid-wicket region for a couple.

It is a nice solid drive. Well attacked by the Pakistani skipper. Full and outside off, Aiden leans forward and drives it through the covers. It is to the left of Babar, at mid off, who gets there and stops it. A single. And that brings up the 50-run partnership between these two.
Fullish and outside off, kept out to mid off.
Good length ball around the off stump area, Aiden stabs it down to mid on.
Length delivery on top of the stumps, Aiden Markram pushes it back to the bowler.
Outside off, dabbed to the off side. The partnership is now worth 49.

Well played. And well fielded as well. Shortish length ball around the off stump area, Rassie goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket. A fielder gives chase and dives ahead of the ropes. Keeps it down to a couple.
Looped up, on the off pole channel, defended to the off side.
FOUR! That is a good shot. He picked it up well. Gets down to the ball which was on a length and kept low. Slog sweeps it over the mid-wicket region.
Flatter and around the off stump, Aiden rocks back and works it through point. Crosses.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Looped up on middle and off, AM prods forward in defence.
Leg side. There is protection in the deep though. Angles in a fullish length delivery on the pads, Aiden Markram clips it down to the fine leg region and gets to the other end. Will retain strike.
On a fullish length and around the off stump line, Markram jumps and keeps it out on the off side.
Fullish and outside the off stump, left alone.
Fullish length and on the pads, flicked down ahead of fine leg and the batters exchange ends.
Fullish length ball, poked through cover-point and the batsmen exchange ends. No ball called. Overstepping.
Fullish length delivery, Aiden is solid in his defence.
That is a terrific line to start. The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Will Nauman Ali continue from the other end? Or will it be a seamer? It is Shaheen Shah Afridi from the other end. The ball is 43 overs old. Expect him to get some reverse swing...
Comes forward, then goes back and keeps this fuller ball out on the leg side.
Loops this very full and outside the off pole line, Rassie leans forward and drives it through the covers.
Works it with the turn through cover-point. Takes a single.
Looped up delivery outside the off pole, Aiden comes forward but ends up leaving it.
On leg, clipped wide of short leg.
A bit of a loosener. Short and outside off, cut through cover-point. Just the single though. Will rotate strike still.

Back for the final session then. The Pakistani players are near the ropes, in a huddle. Done with that, they move on to take their respective positions on the field. The South African batters too make their way out. The pitch is wearing down. Yasir Shah to continue after the break. He is bowling towards the Pavilion End.
... Day 3, Session 3...

Now, coming to the final session of the day, the Saffas still trail by 74 runs. They will want to turn that deficit to a lead, at the end of the Day. The hosts, whereas, would be looking to come out and break this stand and push their counterparts on the back foot, with a couple of wickets. An interesting final session of play awaits on Day 3. Join us shortly for the same.

Since then, the duo of Markram and van der Dussen have really battled it out there and made sure that there were no casualties until the Tea break, at the very least. They have scored at a very brisk pace and at one point, South Africa went 100 deliveries since they scored a boundary. But they have made the bowlers toil and work hard, if they were to sniff any chances. Yasir bowled well and tested the batters but was not able to add any more wickets to his tally, in this session.

South Africa's session, you would say. Agreed, they have not cut down the deficit by a lot but looking at the way they have batted so far, they have shown that they are ready to show their grit and play their way. The second session started off nicely enough for Pakistan as they broke the opening pair as Yasir, who was bowling well and making the ball dance sent Elgar packing.

NOT OUT! No run out on the last ball before Tea then. Fullish length delivery on the pads, Rassie clips it down to short fine leg. He comes down, hesitantly, for a single. But Aiden Markram confidently asks him to rush on and move to the non-striker's end. AM himself hustles to the striker's end as the fielder there, collects and throws it to the keeper's end. Scores a direct hit and the Pakistan players appeal for a run out. It is taken upstairs by the square leg umpire, however, one replay is enough to confirm that the batsman grounded his bat well inside the crease there. WITH THAT, IT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 3!
The third umpire is called into play to check this run out appeal. Replays roll in and it is clearly seen that Markram's bat is well grounded as the bails come off. Will be not out.
Nauman loops this on the middle pole line, blocked to the leg side.
Loopy and on off and middle, defended to short leg.
Comes forward to this one and defends it back on the turf.
This time it is flatter and around the off stump zone. Rassie gets across and back and keeps that one out.
Loopy and outside the off pole, RvdD leans forward and drives that to the covers region.
Loopy ball on off and middle, a dead bat defense from Markram, onto the crease.
Fullish and outside the off pole zone, dabbed to the off side and Aiden says 'no' to his partner.
This is some good batting from AM here. Old-fashioned, basically. It is on the pads and he lets it be. Wears it on his pads.
This time he pads this one to the off side.
On middle, Aiden Markram taps it to the off side, safely, off the leading edge, as he looked to work it on the on side.
Short length ball outside the off stump area, Rassie van der Dussen rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket. A fielder gives chase and keeps it out, in the deep. Three taken though.
Once again he attacks the stumps. Markram stays on the back foot and defends it out.
On off, blocked.
Flatter ball on the pads, van der Dussen camps on the back foot and taps it to the square leg region for a run.
Now he comes forward to the full delivery and defends it back on the track.
Stays deep inside his crease and defends this one out on the leg side.
Loopy delivery on the middle pole line, pushed to the right of the bowler, who gets in that direction and stops it.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
He floats this one too on the off stump area, Rassie works it in front of square on the on side and takes one.
Shah floats this on the off pole area, run down to mid on for a dot.
Gets to the pitch of this full length ball and defends it out.
Outside off, the batter shoulders arms.

'Catch it' is the shout but it was hit with control. Floated, outside the off stump channel, Aiden leans forward and drives it uppish but safely through the covers. Takes a single as it goes to the deep.
'Lovely bowling', says Rizwan. Full and around off and on middle, van der Dussen has just blocked that from his crease.
Fullish and outside the off pole channel, dropped on the off side by Rassie.
Tucks this fullish one to the square leg region and takes a single.
Floated ball on the off stump line, fended out on the off side.
Attacks the stumps with a fuller delivery, defended to the leg side.
Outside off, kept out on the off side.
Camps back and pushes this flatter delivery through the covers for a single.
Floated delivery on the stumps, defended back on the pitch.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
FOUR! That is nicely put away. That is a good shot. First boundary in 100 balls! Short and width on offer, outside the off stump, Aiden goes back and across and cuts it through the point region.
Full and on the middle pole, defended.
Presents the full face of the blade and defends this one out.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Full length delivery, driven to cover.
Fuller in length, outside the off pole, van der Dussen comes forward to defend it. Ends up getting it off the outside edge, safely, to the off side.
Flatter ball outside off, defended to the off side.
Comes on the front foot and blocks this one out.
Fuller in length and on off and middle, Rassie strides forward in defence.

EDGED...DROPPED! Babar Azam is the culprit on this occasion. It was not on the easier side but it should still have been taken. Floats this one up around the middle pole, turns away as Aiden looks to push this to the off side. He can only induce an outside edge and the ball goes to the right of Azam, who dives but is not able to get his hands under the ball. A big, big chance to scalp the second wicket goes begging.
Another solid defense is offered by Markram.
Defended to the cover region.
Flatter and around off, keeps a touch low as well. AM works this one to deep point. They run well to come back for the second run as well.
Flatter and around off, Aiden looks for the defensive push away but gets beaten as the ball spins away sharply and into Rizwan's mitts.
Full and floated on middle, Aiden pushes it back towards Yasir, who mimes a throw back.
Loopy and on leg, van der Dussen pushes this one back onto the turf.
Does exactly what he did on the last delivery.
Shows the full face of the bat and blocks this one out.
Full and tossed up on middle and leg, Rassie taps this one to short leg.
On off, pushed to covers.
Full and floated on middle, Aiden nudges this one towards square leg for a single. 80 balls since the last boundary. It's been quite a longgggg time now.
Nauman Ali is back. Had just a brief spell of 2 overs before Lunch. Let's see how he goes now. Will be interesting to see how the Saffas tackle him...
Tossed up and on middle. van der Dussen is solid in his defense. 2 runs off the 33rd over.
On off, blocked.

EDGY. Flighted and on off, Markram comes on the front foot and looks for the defensive push away, on the off side, but the ball spins away and takes the outer half of the blade, goes to point. A single.
Tossed up and on middle, van der Dussen whips this one towards the mid-wicket region for a single.
Flighted and outside the off pole, Rassie just lets this one be and Rizwan collects.
Goes on his back foot and fends this one out.
Another good length delivery, AM tucks this one to mid-wicket. After bowling two maidens, Ashraf has finally conceded a run in this over.
Blocks this one with a straight bat towards the mid on region.
On a good length and around off, Aiden works this one to the leg side.
Pushes this one towards the cover region for a quick single.
Around the off pole on a good length, Rassie, again keeps this one out.
Angles in a length delivery around the off pole, Rassie defends this one.
Short and around off, Markram taps this one to the point region.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
On off, Aiden keeps this one out.
Loopy and outside off, spins away as Aiden leaves it alone.
Comes on his front foot and defends this one out solidly.
Flat, on off and middle, pushed to the mid on region.
On the pads to Rassie, he tucks it safely on the on side.
Fullish length ball outside the off pole line, dabbed back to the bowler.
Fuller in length delivery on the stumps, defended.
Fullish length delivery outside the off pole, poked to the off side.
This one seams in, towards the woodwork, Rassie van der Dussen gets his front pad out of the way and manages to fend it out.
Short length delivery around the off pole line, clipped to the leg side.
Fuller in length delivery, outside off, Aiden strikes it firmly and Azhar Ali, at covers, does well to keep it out again.

'Catch it' is the call but Azhar actually does well there. Fuller in length ball outside the off pole, Aiden gets forward and drives it firmly. Azhar, at cover, does well to dive and stop that. Saved what looked like a certain boundary.
Flat delivery, just outside the off pole zone, van der Dussen rocks back and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Strides forward and pushes this fuller length delivery, which was around the off stump area, to the right of the spinner. Yasir gets there and stops it.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside the off pole area, Rassie stays inside his crease but ends up leaving it.
Angles in a good length delivery on off and middle, defended back to Faheem.
Short of a length delivery around the off stump channel, Markram stands tall and drives but finds the man at cover there.
Full length ball on off, driven down to mid on.
This one is wide outside the off stump channel, Aiden goes after it but misses. The ball kept low and sneaked under his flashing bat.
Fullish length ball around the off pole channel, the South African strides forward in defence.
Fullish length delivery on top of the middle pole, AM is solid in his block. Has looked good throughout, so far.
Faheem Ashraf has the ball in his grasp now.
Comes from 'over the wicket and bowls a straighter one, outside the off stump line, Rassie van der Dussen strides forward but ends up leaving it.
Full length delivery on the pads, van der Dussen lets that be and gets hit on the pads.
On off and middle, pushed down to mid on.
On the pads, padded away again, this time to the off side.
Pads this delivery away back on the pitch.
Flatter delivery on the off stump, Rassie rocks back and clips it to the leg side. Yasir is bowling well here.

Time for some DRINKS. A good even half session of play for both the teams. Both of them have done well enough but none has grabbed the first hour of the second session by the throat. The decision to bring on Yasir Shah has worked well and he is generating a lot of spin on this surface. He also broke the opening stand for the visitors and Pakistan will look at him for a few more wickets. South Africa, on the other hand, will be looking to see off the remaining half of the session unscathed and will look to cut the deficit down even more.
Outside off, left alone.

Back of a length delivery around the off pole line, Markram stands tall and punches it to the covers region but a fielder there dives well and keeps it out. Aiden Markram wanted a single but seeing that the fielder there stopped it, he decides against it.
Nicely played. Nicely bowled as well. Full length ball around the off pole, it kept low as it approached Aiden. He is able to bring his bat down in time and defend it out.
Full length delivery on middle and leg, clipped to the man at short mid-wicket.
Fullish length delivery on the stumps, Markram pushes it back to the bowler who collects and mimes a throw back, to the sticks at the keeper's end. Makram sways away then.
Length delivery outside off, Aiden stands tall and drives it to cover.
A dot to end a fine over from Yasir. Flighted on leg, van der Dussen comes on his front foot and pads this one away to the off side.
On middle and leg, van der Dussen tucks this one to the leg side.
Loopy on leg, Aiden sweeps this one to the fine leg region for a single.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

BEAUTYYYY! What a delivery. That turned very, very sharply. Flighted on leg, it lands on the rough and spins away sharply as Aiden went onto his back foot looking to block. Beats his outside edge and goes to Rizwan.
Short and on leg, spins back into the right-hander, Rassie tucks this one to mid-wicket for a single.
Flicks this one to the mid-wicket region but finds the fielder there. Just the solitary run off the over.
Angles in a good length delivery around the off pole, Aiden pushes this one with a straight blade towards the mid off region.
Length and around off, keeps low as well this time, but Markram plays this one really well as he keeps this one out towards the backward point region.
Another length ball on off, Aiden blocks.
On the pads, tucked to the square leg region for a single.
Good length delivery around off, nips back in ever-so-slightly, Rassie keeps his eyes on the ball and keeps it out.
Hasan Ali (6-0-22-0) comes on to bowl now.
Floated and on off, Markram comes forward looking to block this one, but the ball takes the outer half of the blade and goes to the point region.
Loopy and on off, AM punches this one to covers.
Flicks this one to the right of mid on for a quick run.
On middle, flicked to short leg again.
Floats one up on middle, van der Dussen tucks this one to the short leg fielder.
Flighted around off, kept out.
Length and around off, Aiden pushes this one to the mid-wicket region.
Short of a length and around off and middle, Aiden hops and blocks this one out.
Review time! We have a player review for lbw and Aiden is the man in question. Let's see what technology has to say...

NOT OUT! Review lost. A poor one taken by Pakistan. Not a very good review. Shortish length delivery down the leg side, keeping low. Markram looks to flick that but misses and is hit on the pads. There is a loud appeal from Shaheen and the Pakistanis for a LBW but the umpire stands his ground. Afridi starts to walk back but then, skipper Azam flashes the 'T'. It is taken upstairs. No bat there and in comes Ball Tracker. It says that the ball was missing the stumps and going well down the leg side.
Attacks the stumps with a fullish one. Dabbed to the leg side.
Full length ball on off and middle, poked down to mid on.
Fullish length ball outside off, defended to the off side.
Fuller leg break landing outside off, left alone.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Flat, outside off, slapped to the cover region for one run.
Flighted and around off, pushed to the covers region.
Skips down the track and does what he did on the last delivery.
Prods forward and blocks this one, does Aiden.
On the pads again, tucked to square leg. The batters take off for the run and the fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end and hits as well but Aiden was in.
FOUR! Gets it nice and fine and past the ropes. Shaheen bowls this slightly behind the good length and on the pads, Markram hops and tickles this one to the fine leg region for a boundary.
Length and around the off pole, Aiden pushes this one towards point.
Shortish and around off, van der Dussen pulls this one to the deep mid-wicket region for a single.
Ohhh...that took off slightly as well. A back of a length ball around off, takes off as it hits the deck, it hits his bat on the handle and goes to the leg side, as Rassie looked to play at that.
Afridi dishes out a good length delivery around off, Rassie pushes this to the mid on region.
Off the edge there. Tossed up ball on middle and leg, van der Dussen comes forward to block but ends up getting it off the inner half. It goes to the man at 45, to his right. A single.
Flighted leg break, around off, left alone.
That is nicely played. Leans forward to the floated ball which was outside off. Pushes it through the covers and gets a couple as mid off runs to the ball and fetches it.
Fuller and on middle and leg, Rassie presses forward and fends it out safely on the off side.
Comes forward to the fuller ball this time and pokes it safely to short leg.
Flatter and on middle and off, Rassie goes back and defends it out.
Fullish length ball around off, defended down to mid on.
Shortish and around off, Aiden hops and keeps that out.
On the pads, clipped to deep backward square leg for one. 50 comes up for the South Africans.
Short of a length and outside off, dabbed to the off side.
Fullish and seaming in towards off and middle, defended down to mid on.
Fullish and around off and middle, Markram works it to square leg off the inner half, for a single.
A wicket maiden over for Shah. He tosses it on off and middle, Rassie van der Dussen pushes it down to mid off.
Flighted around off, van der Dussen comes on the front foot and taps it to the off side.
Comes forward and defends the fuller ball out again.
Floated ball on the off pole line, defended to the on side.
Full and outside off, Rassie prods forward and blocks it.
Who will walk out to bat now? Rassie van der Dussen? Yes, it is him.

OUT! CAUGHT! Yasir has the first breakthrough. Elgar needs to depart now. This is the risk of sweeping across the line when there is rough outside the off pole. Dean Elgar gets across and down and looks to sweep this fullish length delivery. He though ends up getting this off his gloves. It seems to be falling beside the batsman, on the off side, but Mohammad Rizwan, watches the ball, and dives forward to take a stunning catch. The players appeal but Dean Elgar is already on his bike. The umpire then raises his finger.
The South African physio has arrived, again. He is having a look at Dean. Looks like Elgar is still uncomfortable out there. But he is a tough man and is set to continue.
Fullish length and on off and middle, blocked on the off side.

This is a good response from Elgar. Clears his front leg and strokes this shortish ball through the covers. Cover-point and mid off give chase. It does not get to the boundary and hence they run three here.
This is good bowling here. Shortish and around off, Dean swivels inside his crease and does not offer a shot there. The ball though, takes the bottom part of his bat and falls safely on the off side.
Slower delivery, shortish and outside off, Dean Elgar goes for the pull shot but misses. Hmm... looks like he has changed his mind to attack every ball, by the looks of it.
FOUR! Good shot. Short and width on offer, outside off, Dean Elgar lets out a cracking cut shot and gets it through the point region for a boundary.
Shortish length ball around the off pole channel, Elgar swivles inside his crease and pulls it but finds mid-wicket there.
Another testing over comes to an end. Shorter on off, kept out.
Full and outside off, blocked to the off side.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

A huge shout for a LBW but it is not given. Fullish length ball around the off stump line, Aiden Markram gets across but ends up leaving it. Gets hit on the pads and there is a loud appeal for the lbw. But the umpire shakes his head. Yasir, Rizwan, and Babar, have a long chat. The bowler is convinced and wants to take the review but the keeper feels otherwise. In the end, the time lapses and they do not go for the review. Good decision, by the looks of it, as it would go onto miss the stumps.
BEATEN! There you go! How do you play that? Yasir Shah lands the leg break around the off stump, it pitches and moves away just. Beats Markram's outside edge as he prodded forward to defend.
Flatter delivery on middle and leg, clipped to the mid-wicket region.
Shortish length delivery around the off pole line, Dean jumps and keeps it out well.

The physio is coming out to the middle to examine Elgar here. The spray is out. Let's hope he is good to continue here. Looks to be in real pain. Well, he is getting ready to take strike again. That is good news for South Africa then, atleast for now.

Suddenly, you see one that has taken off. Shaheen lands it on a length and around off, it pitches and comes back in sharply. Takes Dean Elgar by surprise. He swivles and looks to let it go but the ball takes him, flush on the gloves. 'Catch it' is the shout but the ball falls safely on the leg side. He seems to be in some pain here. Has sat down.

FOUR! Well, that is a well-timed shot. Just using the pace. A typical drive. Length delivery, outside the off pole line, Dean Elgar stands tall and just thumps it through cover-point. A fielder gives chase, but in vain.
Short length delivery outside the off pole, Elgar lets it be.
Fullish length delivery outside off, Dean is solid in his defence.
Full length delivery around off, driven down to mid off.
Will Hasan Ali continue from the other end? No, it is the primary seamer, Shaheen Afridi, who is back on now. So, leg spinner from one end and pacer from the other.
Flatter delivery around off and middle, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
'Very well bowled' says Mohammad Rizwan. Fullish length delivery outside off, defended off the back foot, to the off side.
Very full length delivery on middle, Markram manages to dig it out.
On off and middle, clipped to the man at short leg.
Full toss on middle and leg, bunted down to mid on. Elgar wanted a single. Aiden comes down but manages to send his non-striker back as the fielder got to the ball there.

We are back for the second session then, at Karachi. The sun is shining brightly and the National Stadium looks pretty glowing. Out walk the Pakistan players then, followed by South Africa's openers, Dean Elgar and Aiden Markram. Looks like Yasir might start with the ball in the second session. Yes, he is being brought on straightaway. He should be getting some turn off the track. Here comes Shah...
... Day 3, Session 2...

In response to this, the openers of the visitors have done well so far to fend off everything that the Pakistani bowling attack has thrown at them. Elgar and Markram did not score runs at a quick pace but they have done well to add 37 before the Lunch break and also have cut the deficit to 121 runs. They will be looking to stay out there for as long as they can. Pakistan will be hoping to come back and scalp a few quick wickets to put their counterparts on the back foot. Which team takes the second session? Join us in a short while to find out.

An interesting session of play comes to an end. Both the team would be slightly pleased with how things have panned out. Even though, South Africa took time to scalp the last wicket. They have started off well with the bat in hand. Pakistan came into his day with 2 wickets in hand. They lost Hasan Ali early on and then the duo of Yasir Shah and Nauman Ali did well to stitch a 55-run stand for the last wicket to propel Pakistan to 378, and also ended with a lead of 158 to their name.
Back of a length and around off, tapped to point. IT IS LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Ali digs in a short ball on off, Dean pulls this one to the backward square leg region for a couple of runs.
WIDE. Too short and on middle and leg, Dean just ducks under this one. Wided by the umpire.
Slower good length ball around off, DE pushes this one to the off side.
Outside off, left alone.
PLAY AND A MISS. On a length and outside off, Dean looks to block this one out but the ball zips past the outside edge into Rizwan's mitts.
Length and on middle, pushed to mid on.
Tossed up and around off, Aiden works this to the mid off region.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! A misfield from Azhar Ali and this one will be a boundary! Flighted and outside off, Markram punches this one through the cover region where Ali fumbles and lets this one through, to go to the ropes.
Flighted and around off, Aiden looks to block this one out but the ball takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
Floated and full outside off, Dean strokes this one through point for a single.
Blocked off the front foot by Elgar.
Outside off, left alone.

An appeal for lbw but to no avail. A back of a length and on middle and leg, Aiden looks to tuck this one away but misses to get hit on the pads. Hasan appeals but no says the umpire. Hasan looks at Rizwan and confirms that this looked to be going down the leg side.
Short of a length and around off, AM pushes this one towards point.
Three! Back of a length and outside off, Dean punches this one through the cover-point region and picks up three runs.
Pushed to the cover region this time.
BEATEN. On a good length and outside off, Dean looks to block this one out but the ball zips past the outside edge and goes to the keeper.
A maiden to start off with. Floats it up nicely around off, kept out.
Flat, on middle, clipped to the mid on region.
Flighted around off, AM pushes this one to the off side.
Shortish and around off, Aiden works this one to the cover region.
Floated around off, blocked.
Short and on off, Aiden pushes this one to the mid on region.
Time for some spin. Nauman Ali is introduced into the attack.
On the pads, tucked to the mid-wicket region.
On a good length and around off, Dean gets behind the line of the ball and defends.
The physio is out into the middle now, having a look at Dean Elgar. They will have their mandatory concussion check. He is fine to continue.

OUCH! Right on the helmet this time. A short of a length delivery around off, zips in off the surface and the bounce gets slightly bigger on Dean as he looks to pull. He misses his stroke and gets hit on the helmet. Hasan Ali comes across and makes sure that Elgar is alright.
Around off on a good length, DE keeps this one out.
Around off on a good length, Dean looks to push this one to the off side but the ball takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
On off, tucked to mid-wicket. The batters set off for the single. The fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. Replays show that Aiden was safe, even if he had hit.
Length and on off, AM pushes this one to mid-wicket for a single.
Full and around off, pushed to covers for a single.
Short and on the body, Aiden hops and tucks this one through backward square leg. Gets to the other end.
Bouncer on off, Markram sways away from the line of the ball and lets this one through.
Good length on off, Aiden pushes this one to the covers.
Short of a length, on off, tapped to point.

FOUR! Lovely punch. What a nice way to round off this over. On a good length and around off, Elgar creams this one through the extra cover region and the ball wins the race to the ropes, even though a fielder gave it a chase.
On middle, tucked to the leg side, but straight to the fielder.
Length on off, pushed to covers.
Short of a length ball on middle, clipped to square leg. One more run.
Flicked to the mid-wicket region for a single.
Back of a length and on middle, clipped to the mid-wicket region.
Short of a length and around off, Markram blocks. South Africa trail by 142 runs.
NO BALL. On a length and around off, pushed to mid on. Another no ball as Afridi has overstepped his line.
Length and around off, Aiden pushes it back to the bowler.
Quick run. Length on off, Dean pushes this one to point and the batters take a quick run.
Length and around off, tapped towards point.
Gets his bat down and defends this one out.
Short of a length and around off, Dean pushes this one to the off side.
Good length and on off, Aiden pushes it back to the bowler.
Length and around off, pushed to covers.
FOUR! Short of a length and on middle, Aiden clips this one through fine leg and fetches a boundary for himself. Third one of the South African innings.
Solid defense offered by Markram, this time around.
Back of a length and around off, Aiden pushes this one to the mid on region.
Short of a length and on leg, tucked to fine leg for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Aiden leaves this one alone, for the keeper to collect.

NOT OUT! A good review from Aiden and he survives. A back of a length ball around middle and off, Markram looks to tuck this one away but he misses and gets rapped on the pads. An appeal and the umpire obliges, raising his finger. Markram goes for the review straightaway. Ultra Edge shows no bat. Ball Tracker shows that this one was pitching outside the leg pole.The on-field decision has been overturned.
South Africa review early on! Markram has been given out for this lbw appeal. Looks to be pitching outside leg. The decision has been overturned.
Outside off, left alone.
Gets his bat down and defends it back towards Shaheen. Will also be a No Ball as Shaheen had overstepped.
Just around that good length and outside the off pole, Aiden just lets it be.
Outside off, good length, slapped to covers.
A stifled appeal. Back of a length and around off, Dean looks to leave but it hits his thigh pad and goes to the keeper. An appeal but turned down.

FOUR! CREAMED! Elgar opens his account in the game as well. On a good length and outside off, Elgar plays this one through the cover region and there is no use running behind this one. Will be a boundary.
Good length and around off, pushed towards the bowler.
Length and around off, pushed towards covers.
Dean has just blocked that from his crease.
Ali starts off with a good length delivery outside off, Dean just leaves this one alone.
Who will bowl from the other end? Hasan Ali, it is.
Back of a length and around off, Aiden keeps this one out. Just 4 off the opening over.
Outside off, left alone.
Similar delivery as the last ball, Aiden offers the same shot as he did on the last ball. Which is basically no shot.
Outside off again on a good length, Aiden lets it be.
On a good length outside off, Aiden leaves this one alone.
FOUR! South Africa and Markram are underway! Back of a length ball and outside off, Markram punches this one through the cover-point region and the ball speeds away to the ropes.
Right then. We are back for the second innings. The batters for South Africa, Dean Elgar and Aiden Markram stride out into the middle. Shaheen Afridi to begin with the ball. Here he comes...
